1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate letter and line spacing, though it is not verifiably a specialist dyslexia-friendly font.

2.why: No italics, all-caps, or dense text blocks appear anywhere; all headings, labels and buttons use sentence case.

3.why: Every screen is a single-column, mobile-width layout with large inputs and full-width buttons that remain clearly readable.

4.why: Instructions are single short plain sentences, e.g. 'Sign in first. Then we will help you add your authenticator.' and 'We can send one short code to your email or phone.'

5.why: Expected input is exemplified via the placeholders 'name@example.com' on the email field and 'Example: 123456' on the verification code field.

6.why: No observed screen requires reading more than one or two short sentences to proceed.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control appears in any screenshot, the 6-digit code must be typed by hand, and the steps that would display secrets or backup codes were never reached.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is visible in any of the six screenshots, and the authenticator setup step is marked incomplete.

9.why: The form uses ordinary-looking email, password and code fields, but autofill or password-manager support can be neither confirmed nor refuted from the images alone.

10.why: A 'Step X of 4' banner tops every screen and the primary action is a large solid-blue button, with a yellow focus outline making the current action stand out.

11.why: The code-entry screen shows two competing solid-blue primary-styled buttons ('Send code' and 'Check code') plus a 'Send a new code' button, so more than one main action is present at once.

12.why: Status banners plainly state what happened and what comes next after each action, e.g. 'Signed in. Next, check it is you.' and 'A code was sent. Enter the 6 numbers when you are ready.'

13.why: Retry and re-request are supported via the 'Send a new code' button and an error message inviting another attempt, but no reveal/hide toggle for the password or codes is visible.

14.why: The only error shown, 'That code did not match. Check the 6 numbers or send a new code.', states the problem and the fix in neutral, non-blaming language.

15.why: Banners repeatedly say 'Enter it when you are ready' and no countdown or timer is visible on any screen, though the actual code-expiry period cannot be verified from static screenshots.
